ayat.theme: Joseph interprets cupbearer restoration and baker execution
ayat.comparison_note: Close narrative parallel; Qur'an says birds eat from executed prisoner's head, Genesis describes birds eating his flesh; mode of execution translation varies.

ayat.theme: Joseph asks freed prisoner to mention him; forgotten and remains incarcerated
ayat.comparison_note: Close sequence parallel; Genesis specifies a request to Pharaoh and later two years, Qur'an says several years and uses a theological explanation of forgetting.

ayat.theme: Ruler dreams of seven fat and seven lean cattle and green and dry grain ears
ayat.comparison_note: Distinctive shared double dream; Genesis has cows emerging from Nile and seven healthy ears swallowed by thin ears; Qur'an has seven lean cows eating fat ones and green/dry ears.

ayat.theme: Court notables cannot interpret the dream
ayat.comparison_note: Narrative parallel; Genesis mentions magicians and wise men, Qur'an reports dismissal as confused dreams.

ayat.theme: Freed prisoner recalls Joseph and volunteers to obtain interpretation
ayat.comparison_note: Close narrative function but different order of access: Genesis cupbearer recounts Joseph to Pharaoh, Qur'an offers to be sent to Joseph.

dossier.scope: Joseph's prison interpretations, forgotten request, Pharaoh's double dream and court response
dossier.chronology: Genesis is a pre-Islamic Jewish literary tradition; distinguish ancient composition/redaction from medieval Masoretic codices and surviving Greek/Syriac witnesses; exact dates pending bibliographic verification.
dossier.comparison: Qur'an 12:41 and Genesis 40:12-22 both predict the restoration of a drink-server and death of a second prisoner. Qur'an 12:42 and Genesis 40:14-15,23 recount Joseph's request to be remembered and the prisoner's forgetting. Qur'an 12:43 and Genesis 41:1-7 share seven healthy and seven lean cattle plus seven good and seven poor ears of grain; Genesis supplies Nile and sequential dream details. Qur'an 12:44-45 and Genesis 41:8-13 both portray court inability to interpret and the former prisoner's recollection, but differ in whether the official tells the ruler or goes to Joseph. No evidence here establishes direct borrowing.
